newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: New hope for release of Colombian rebel captives.
newsitem.headline: New hope for release of Colombian rebel captives.

text.p: Hopes soared that 60 Colombian soldiers could soon be freed more than eight months after being taken prisoner by leftist rebels following the release of new video footage of the captives on Sunday.
The Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC), the country's largest guerrilla army, sent video footage of the soldiers to the NTC-TV news programme.

The government welcomed the film, thought to have been shot in early March, as a sign of FARC's "good faith" and a hint the insurgents could be preparing to release the troops they captured in the southern jungles of Colombia on Aug. 30.
The seven-minute video showed the soldiers in apparent good health standing at attention outside a number of tents in a jungle clearing.
"This is an important message that shows the good intentions of the FARC and offers a new ray of hope," Defence Minister Gilberto Echeverri told reporters.

The soldiers were taken prisoner and some 30 others were killed when a 400-strong FARC column overran the Las Delicias military base in Putumayo province -- an attack that marked the start of one of the bloodiest guerrilla offensives in more than three decades of armed uprising.

Previous government attempts to win the release of the captives have failed. But after four months of deadlock speculation is high that the soldiers, many of them raw recruits from peasant families, could soon walk free.

Last week the government formally appointed a representative, Jose Noe Rios, to negotiate an end to the prisoner crisis while the FARC said it had named three delegates to discuss conditions for the handover.
Commander of the armed forces Gen. Manuel Jose Bonett said that he had ordered the suspension of all operations to search for the captives while negotiations were in progress.
